properties.name: Niger River
properties.summary: West Africa's principal river; enters Nigeria from Niger Republic and flows south to the Niger Delta.
properties.description: The Niger is the third-longest river in Africa. Inside Nigeria it passes through the northwest, the Middle Belt confluence at Lokoja, and fans into the world's third-largest delta. It supports hydropower (Kainji, Jebba, Shiroro on tributaries), inland navigation, and the oil-bearing delta wetlands.
properties.lengthNote: About 1,300 km of the course lies in Nigeria
properties.sourceNote: Guinea Highlands (outside Nigeria); enters Nigeria near the Niger Republic border in Kebbi
properties.mouthNote: Gulf of Guinea via the Niger Delta (Nun, Forcados and many creeks)
properties.economy: Hydropower, inland waterways, fisheries, irrigation, and the delta petroleum basin.
properties.ecology: Floodplain agriculture (fadama), manatee and fish diversity, mangrove delta.
properties.significance: Kainji Dam, Lokoja confluence, Niger Delta outlet, historic trade corridor.

properties.name: Benue River
properties.summary: The Niger's largest tributary; enters from Cameroon and meets the Niger at Lokoja.
properties.description: The Benue drains the Cameroon highlands and the Nigerian Middle Belt. Seasonal floods fertilise yam and rice plains in Adamawa, Taraba, and Benue. Makurdi is the main urban crossing. The confluence at Lokoja is one of West Africa's great geographic landmarks.
properties.mouthNote: Joins the Niger at Lokoja, Kogi State
properties.economy: Irrigation, fisheries, sand mining, and a historic (now limited) inland waterway.
properties.ecology: Seasonal floodplains; hippo and fish habitats; erosion on sandy banks.
properties.significance: Agricultural belt, Makurdi bridge, confluence at Lokoja.

properties.name: Cross River
properties.summary: Eastern river forming much of the Cameroon border before the Gulf of Guinea.
properties.description: The Cross (Oyono) drains rainforest of Cross River State and western Cameroon. It is associated with Cross River National Park, Calabar port access, and high freshwater biodiversity. Seasonal floods affect Ogoja–Ikom–Calabar corridors.
properties.mouthNote: Cross River estuary near Calabar, Gulf of Guinea
properties.economy: Port access, fisheries, timber hinterland, border trade.
properties.ecology: Rainforest, primates (including Cross River gorilla in the wider basin), estuary mangroves.
properties.significance: Rainforest ecology, Calabar port, international border.

properties.name: Kaduna River
properties.summary: Major tributary of the Niger flowing through Kaduna and Niger states.
properties.description: The Kaduna (named from 'crocodile' in Hausa, Kada) gives Kaduna city its name. It joins the Niger in Niger State. Shiroro Dam is a major hydro station on the system.
properties.economy: Hydropower (Shiroro), urban water, fisheries.
properties.significance: Kaduna city namesake, Shiroro hydro, joins Niger.

properties.name: Sokoto River
properties.summary: Principal river of north-western Nigeria; feeds the Rima and Niger systems.
properties.description: The Sokoto–Rima basin is the agricultural heart of the far northwest. Seasonal flooding supports irrigation schemes and grazing. The Bakolori and Goronyo dams regulate parts of the system.
properties.mouthNote: Niger River via the Rima in Kebbi / Niger
properties.economy: Irrigation (Bakolori, Goronyo), millet and rice, livestock.
properties.significance: Sokoto basin irrigation, seasonal flooding, Hausa–Fulani heartland.

properties.name: Gongola River
properties.summary: Major Benue tributary draining the Bauchi–Gombe plateau and Adamawa foothills.
properties.description: The Gongola flows through northeastern Nigeria before joining the Benue. Its basin supports rice, sorghum, and livestock in a savanna–Sahel transition zone. Seasonal floods shape farming calendars in Gombe and Adamawa.
properties.economy: Irrigation, rice, livestock, sand mining.
properties.significance: Benue feeder, northeastern agricultural belt.

properties.name: Ogun River
properties.summary: Southwestern river flowing through Ogun State toward the Lagos Lagoon.
properties.description: The Ogun drains Yoruba highlands and feeds the Lagos Lagoon system with the Osun. It supports Abeokuta's water supply, quarrying, and peri-urban agriculture along its banks.
properties.economy: Urban water, quarrying, agriculture, lagoon fisheries.
properties.ecology: Forest–savanna transition; urban pollution pressure downstream.
properties.significance: Abeokuta water source, Lagos Lagoon feeder.

properties.name: Hadejia River
properties.summary: Northeastern river feeding the Hadejia–Nguru wetlands and Komadugu Yobe system.
properties.description: The Hadejia is central to one of Nigeria's largest seasonal wetland complexes. Flood recession farming and fishing depend on its pulse. Upstream dams and climate change have altered flow regimes.
properties.economy: Flood-recession farming, fishing, pastoralism.
properties.ecology: Seasonal wetlands; bird habitat; drought sensitivity.
properties.significance: Hadejia–Nguru wetlands, Sahel agriculture.

properties.name: Komadugu Yobe
properties.summary: Northeastern river system flowing toward Lake Chad via the Hadejia–Nguru wetlands.
properties.description: The Komadugu Yobe (Yobe River) drains the Chad basin fringe of Nigeria. It connects to seasonal channels toward Lake Chad and supports transhumance corridors in Borno and Yobe.
properties.economy: Pastoralism, recession farming, cross-border trade toward Chad.
properties.ecology: Sahel channels; Lake Chad basin dependency.
properties.significance: Lake Chad feeder system, Sahel livelihoods.

properties.name: Imo River
properties.summary: Major river of the southeast flowing through Imo toward Rivers State and the delta.
properties.description: The Imo drains the rain-fed southeast and feeds delta creeks. It is important for oil-palm landscapes, local fisheries, and as a cultural boundary river among Igbo communities.
properties.economy: Oil palm, fisheries, sand, local transport.
properties.significance: Oil palm belt, local fisheries, delta tributary.

properties.name: Osun River
properties.summary: Sacred Yoruba river flowing through Osun State toward the Lagos lagoon system.
properties.description: The Osun is central to Yoruba cosmology (Ọṣun). The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove on its banks is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Hydrologically it is part of the Ogun–Osun drainage toward the Lagos Lagoon.
properties.economy: Water supply, tourism/festival economy, peri-urban agriculture.
properties.ecology: Sacred grove forest remnant; urban pressure downstream.
properties.significance: Osun-Osogbo heritage, Osogbo festival, Lagos water supply.

properties.name: Anambra River
properties.summary: Important Niger tributary draining Anambra and Enugu states into the main stem.
properties.description: The Anambra (Omambala) is a key southeastern tributary of the Niger. Its floodplains support yam and rice farming and local fisheries. Onitsha sits at its confluence zone with the Niger.
properties.economy: Agriculture, fisheries, sand mining.
properties.significance: Onitsha hinterland, Niger feeder.

properties.name: Nun River
properties.summary: Major Niger distributary carrying a large share of Niger flow to the Atlantic through Bayelsa.
properties.description: The Nun is one of the Niger's primary delta outlets. It is lined with oil infrastructure, riverine settlements, and mangrove. Navigation and pipeline corridors follow its banks. Seasonal flooding shapes Ijaw livelihoods.
properties.economy: Oil logistics, river transport, artisanal fishing.
properties.ecology: Mangrove and freshwater swamp; oil-spill exposure.
properties.significance: Main Niger outlet branch, oil corridor, Ijaw riverine heartland.

properties.name: Forcados River
properties.summary: Western delta channel serving historic Forcados oil terminal and navigation.
properties.description: Forcados was a Royal Niger Company and later oil-export anchorage. The river remains a pipeline and terminal access route in Delta State, with mixed fishing and oil-service traffic.
properties.economy: Crude export logistics, fishing, bunkering-risk waterway.
properties.significance: Forcados oil terminal, pipeline hub, colonial-era ocean outlet.

properties.name: Escravos River
properties.summary: Delta channel serving Warri and the Escravos gas-to-liquids / terminal complex.
properties.description: Escravos ('slaves' in Portuguese, a colonial toponym) is now synonymous with Chevron and gas infrastructure. The waterway links Warri's industrial waterfront to the Bight of Benin.
properties.economy: Gas-to-liquids, terminals, Warri port access.
properties.significance: Escravos GTL, Warri access, western delta energy corridor.

properties.name: Bonny River
properties.summary: Deep channel to Port Harcourt and Bonny Island LNG and oil terminals.
properties.description: The Bonny estuary is Nigeria's premier LNG (NLNG) and a historic Ibani (Bonny) kingdom waterway. Large tankers and LNG carriers use dredged channels. Port Harcourt's port sits upriver.
properties.economy: LNG, crude export, Port Harcourt harbour, oil services.
properties.significance: NLNG Bonny Island, PH port, eastern export gateway.

properties.name: New Calabar River
properties.summary: Creek system west of Port Harcourt used for fisheries and peri-urban waterways.
properties.description: The New Calabar (Kalabari) river system serves Kalabari communities and PH's western waterfront. It is important for artisanal fishing and local transport rather than deep-sea export.
properties.economy: Fisheries, local boats, peri-urban settlement.
properties.significance: Kalabari waterways, PH western creeks.

properties.name: 1 Division (Kaduna)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Kaduna; area of responsibility covers the northwest and parts of the north-central belt.
properties.description: The 1 Division is one of the Nigerian Army's oldest fighting formations. Based in Kaduna, its AOR traditionally covers the northwest states and adjoining north-central areas, including internal security deployments and border defence along the Niger frontier.
properties.economy: Defence garrison, barracks infrastructure, and military logistics hub.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna with distinct harmattan season.
properties.landmarks: ["1 Division Hqs, Kaduna","Kaduna cantonments","Nigerian Defence Academy nearby"]

properties.name: 2 Division (Ibadan)
properties.summary: Headquarters at Ibadan; responsible for the southwest geo-political zone and Kwara.
properties.description: The 2 Division is the Nigerian Army's southwest-facing formation. Its area of responsibility spans the six southwest states plus Kwara, supporting internal security, border patrols with Benin, and national rapid-reaction tasking from Army HQ.
properties.economy: Defence garrison and cantonment services for the southwest region.
properties.landmarks: ["2 Division Hqs, Ibadan","Dodan Barracks links","Southwest cantonments"]

properties.name: 3 Division (Jos)
properties.summary: Headquarters near Jos; covers the north-central plateau and parts of the northeast interior.
properties.description: 3 Division operates from the Jos Plateau, with brigades and forward operating bases extending across Plateau, Nasarawa, Benue, and parts of the northeast corridor. It has historically been engaged in plateau crisis management and Middle Belt internal security.
properties.economy: Defence cantonments, peace-support logistics, and Middle Belt garrison network.
properties.climate: Highland climate on the Jos Plateau; warmer southern sectors.
properties.landmarks: ["3 Division Hqs, Jos","Plateau barracks","Benue valley deployments"]

properties.name: 6 Division (Port Harcourt)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Port Harcourt; area of responsibility covers the Niger Delta states.
properties.description: 6 Division is the Nigerian Army's dedicated formation for the Niger Delta. It supports Joint Task Force (JTF) operations in the oil-producing states, providing internal security and pipeline protection across the south-south.
properties.founded: Created to secure the Niger Delta theatre
properties.economy: Oil-region security, JTF deployments, delta logistics support.
properties.climate: Equatorial; heavy rainfall and mangrove delta.
properties.landmarks: ["6 Division Hqs, Port Harcourt","Delta cantonments","Bonny / Escravos sector coverage"]
properties.highlights: ["Port Harcourt-based Division","Delta oil-region AOR","JTF support formation"]

properties.name: 7 Division (Maiduguri)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Maiduguri; frontline counter-insurgency division for Borno and Yobe.
properties.description: 7 Division was raised specifically for the northeast counter-insurgency theatre. It is the Nigerian Army's principal fighting formation against insurgent groups in Borno, Yobe, and adjoining Lake Chad basin areas, with extensive forward operating bases.
properties.economy: Counter-insurgency garrison, theatre logistics, military-civilian aid coordination.
properties.climate: Sahel; very hot dry season with short rains.
properties.landmarks: ["7 Division Hqs, Maiduguri","Lake Chad sector bases","Northeast theatre FOBs"]

properties.name: 8 Division (Sokoto)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Sokoto; area of responsibility for the far northwest states and Niger border arc.
properties.description: 8 Division is tasked with the far-northwest corridor, covering the Sokoto caliphate heartland and contiguous border states facing Niger. Responsibilities include border defence, anti-banditry operations, and coordination with regional security forces.
properties.founded: Restructured to cover the far northwest frontier and border security corridor
properties.economy: Border security, anti-banditry deployments, caliphate-region garrison.
properties.climate: Sahel; short rains and intense harmattan.
properties.landmarks: ["8 Division Hqs, Sokoto","Niger border FOBs","Far NW cantonments"]

properties.name: 81 Division (Lagos)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Lagos; defends the federal economic capital, seaports, and southwest maritime flank.
properties.description: 81 Division is the Nigerian Army's Lagos-based formation, responsible for the defence of the Lagos metropolis, Apapa and Lekki ports, and the immediate southwest maritime hinterland. It also provides ceremonial and national-capital standby roles.
properties.founded: Lagos garrison restructured as a division-level formation
properties.economy: Lagos garrison, port security forces, state ceremonial duties.
properties.landmarks: ["81 Division Hqs, Lagos","Dodan Barracks heritage","Lekki + Apapa port sectors"]

properties.name: 82 Division (Enugu)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Enugu; area of responsibility covers the southeast and eastern south-south states.
properties.description: 82 Division is the Nigerian Army's formation for the southeast. Based in Enugu, it extends across the five southeast states plus the eastern south-south corridor, handling internal security and the Cameroon border flank near Cross River.
properties.founded: Post-civil-war reorganisation for the eastern theatre
properties.economy: Southeast garrison, border security near Cameroon, eastern corridor deployments.
properties.climate: Tropical; escarpment hills and rainforest fringe.
properties.landmarks: ["82 Division Hqs, Enugu","Southeast cantonments","Cameroon border sector"]
properties.highlights: ["Enugu-based Division","SE + eastern SS AOR","Cameroon border flank"]

properties.name: Guards Brigade (Abuja)
properties.summary: Headquarters in Abuja; elite formation protecting the FCT, presidential villa, and federal institutions.
properties.description: The Guards Brigade is the Nigerian Army's elite capital-guard formation. It is responsible for protecting the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock), National Assembly, Supreme Court, foreign missions, and the wider Abuja Federal Capital Territory. It also mounts state ceremonial parades.
properties.founded: FCT-era elite brigade for Abuja and federal institutions
properties.economy: FCT defence, federal institutions protection, state ceremonial events.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna with cooler nights than the coast.
properties.landmarks: ["Guards Brigade Hqs, Abuja","Aso Rock Presidential Villa","Three Arms Zone coverage"]
properties.highlights: ["Abuja-based Elite Brigade","FCT + federal institutions AOR","State ceremonial role"]

properties.name: Western Naval Command (Lagos)
properties.summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Western Naval Command; controls the Lagos barrier coast and adjoining maritime area.
properties.description: The Western Naval Command is one of the Nigerian Navy's three principal formations, based in the Lagos area with responsibility for the entire western maritime flank including the Lagos Lagoon, Lekki approaches, and Badagry creeks. It hosts key naval bases, jetties, and security assets for the nation's premier port cluster.
properties.economy: Maritime security, naval base infrastructure, coastal patrol.
properties.significance: Defence of Lagos ports, maritime domain awareness, western coast security.
properties.landmarks: ["Western Command HQ","Lagos naval jetties","Apapa / Lekki port defence"]
properties.highlights: ["Western Command HQ","Lagos naval jetties","Apapa / Lekki port defence"]

properties.name: Central Naval Command (Yenagoa / Warri)
properties.summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Central Naval Command; responsible for the Niger Delta maritime flank and delta creeks.
properties.description: The Central Naval Command is the Nigerian Navy's delta-facing formation, operating across the Niger Delta creeks from the Escravos/Forcados terminals to Bonny and the central delta waterways. It coordinates JTF maritime components, anti-piracy, and oil-and-gas infrastructure protection.
properties.economy: Delta maritime security, anti-piracy patrols, oil infrastructure defence.
properties.significance: Niger Delta maritime domain and oil-terminal security command.
properties.landmarks: ["Central Command HQ","Escravos / Forcados sector","Delta creek patrols"]
properties.highlights: ["Central Command HQ","Escravos / Forcados sector","Delta creek patrols"]

properties.name: Eastern Naval Command (Calabar)
properties.summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Eastern Naval Command; covers the Cross River estuary, eastern seaboard, and Cameroon border maritime approaches.
properties.description: The Eastern Naval Command is the Nigerian Navy's formation for the eastern coast, including the Cross River estuary at Calabar, Akwa Ibom coast, and the Bakassi/Cameroon maritime frontier. It supports Calabar Port security and joint border maritime operations.
properties.economy: Eastern seaboard maritime security, Calabar port defence, Cameroon border patrol.
properties.significance: Defence of the eastern coast, Cross River estuary, and Calabar harbour.
properties.landmarks: ["Eastern Command HQ","Calabar naval base","Bakassi / Cameroon frontier"]
properties.highlights: ["Eastern Command HQ","Calabar naval base","Bakassi / Cameroon frontier"]

properties.name: Nigerian Air Force HQ (Abuja)
properties.type: NAF Headquarters & Abuja air defence sector
properties.summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Air Force in Abuja; coordinates national air defence, air operations, and the NAF chain of command.
properties.description: The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) is commanded from its headquarters in the Abuja military cantonment area. It oversees air combat, airlift, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) across all tactical commands. HQ NAF coordinates with the Defence Headquarters and service branches on joint operations.
properties.founded: Established 1964; HQ relocated to Abuja after FCT became seat of government
properties.economy: HQ staff, defence planning, ISR coordination, and joint task-force liaison.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna; cooler nights than coastal Nigeria.
properties.landmarks: ["HQ NAF, Abuja","Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport NAF detachment","Defence Headquarters area"]
properties.highlights: ["Overall NAF command HQ","National air defence coordination","Joint operations HQ"]

properties.name: Tactical Air Command (Makurdi)
properties.type: Tactical Air Command HQ — combat & close air support
properties.summary: NAF Tactical Air Command HQ at Makurdi; leads fighter, ground-attack, and helicopter combat elements for northeast and Middle Belt theatres.
properties.description: The Tactical Air Command (TAC) is the NAF's principal fighting headquarters. Based in Makurdi, Benue State, it controls fighter jets (F-7, Alpha Jet, Super Tucano), attack helicopters, and close air support squadrons that have been heavily used in the northeast counter-insurgency campaign and across Middle Belt internal-security deployments.
properties.founded: NAF Makurdi developed as the tactical fighter hub
properties.economy: Combat air operations, maintenance depots, ordnance, and airbase support services.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna; Benue River valley humidity.
properties.landmarks: ["NAF Base Makurdi / TAC HQ","Benue River bridge approach","Makurdi airbase apron"]
properties.highlights: ["Tactical Air Command HQ","Fighter & attack helicopter fleet","CAS for northeast theatre"]

properties.name: Air Training Command (Kaduna)
properties.summary: NAF Air Training Command in Kaduna; runs flying schools, ground-training colleges, and the NAF military aviation pipeline.
properties.description: The Air Training Command (ATC) headquartered at Kaduna (NAF Base Kaduna) is the NAF's training command. It runs the Nigerian Air Force Academy, 301 Flying Training School, 303/325 training wings, and technical schools for pilots, engineers, air defence, and ground-support trades.
properties.founded: Training command evolved with the expansion of the NAF in the 1970s–80s
properties.economy: Flying instruction, maintenance training, cadet academies, and NAF education services.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna with distinct harmattan season.
properties.landmarks: ["NAF Base Kaduna / ATC HQ","Nigerian Air Force Academy","301 Flying Training School"]
properties.highlights: ["NAF pilot training pipeline","Air Training Command HQ","NAF Academy"]

properties.name: Mobility Command (Yenagoa / Bayelsa)
properties.type: Airlift, maritime patrol, and special-ops mobility command
properties.summary: NAF Mobility Command HQ in the Yenagoa/Port Harcourt axis; runs transport, SAR, and maritime-patrol fixed-wing and rotary assets.
properties.description: Mobility Command (MC) was stood up to unify the NAF's airlift, search-and-rescue (SAR), and maritime domain-awareness fleets. It operates C-130, Dornier 228, King Air, AW109/139 helicopters, and the ATR-42/72 maritime-patrol fleet, with responsibility over the Niger Delta waterways and coastal approaches.
properties.founded: Established to coordinate NAF mobility & maritime assets
properties.economy: Airlift, maritime patrol, medevac, special-forces insertion, coastal SAR.
properties.climate: Equatorial delta; mangrove wetlands, heavy rainfall.
properties.landmarks: ["Mobility Command HQ, Bayelsa","NAF maritime patrol detachments","Niger Delta air logistics"]
properties.highlights: ["Airlift & SAR command","Maritime patrol (ATR fleet)","Delta sector mobility"]

properties.name: Logistics Command (Ikeja / Lagos)
properties.type: Maintenance, supply, and depot logistics command
properties.summary: NAF Logistics Command at Ikeja (Lagos); manages airframe/engine maintenance depots, supply chains, and national-level NAF logistics support.
properties.description: The Logistics Command (LC) headquartered at NAF Base Ikeja (adjacent to Murtala Muhammed International Airport) is the NAF's maintenance-and-supply backbone. It runs the 431 Engineering Group (airframe depot), 435 Maintenance Depot, national supply and ammunition pipelines, and Lagos-area NAF air-transport detachments.
properties.founded: Logistics Command was created to consolidate NAF maintenance & supply
properties.economy: Aircraft maintenance, engine overhaul, supply depots, ordnance, and NAF logistics services.
properties.climate: Tropical monsoon; high humidity and two rainfall peaks.
properties.landmarks: ["NAF Base Ikeja / LC HQ","431 Engineering Group","MMIA NAF liaison & apron"]
properties.highlights: ["Logistics Command HQ","Airframe & engine depot","NAF national supply chain"]
